html:
SMTO-HTTP-0050 — SMTO can't tell if your change reached the other service

GUID: b897e3ad-543e-405f-8e59-fd77c6c224c3
Slug: http-mutation-outcome-unknown
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO sent a request that changes something on another website or service, but the reply was lost or unreadable. The change may or may not have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the Conversation, look at the step that failed to see which service SMTO was contacting and what it was trying to change. Knowing the exact change tells you what to look for on the other service.
  2. Open that website or service yourself and check the item involved, such as a record, ticket, message or file, to see whether the change is already there. The request may have finished even though SMTO never received the answer.
  3. Only if the change is missing, ask the Agent to make it again. If it is already there, tell the Agent so it moves on without repeating it. Repeating a change that already went through could create a duplicate, such as a second order or message.

What success looks like

  • You have confirmed on the other service whether the change happened, and it appears there exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Check whether the earlier action already happened before trying it again; if you can't tell, don't repeat it. Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the other service so they can check its records.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An http.request write (any method other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS) may have reached its target, but the Gateway response was lost, reported effect_unknown, or returned a receipt that failed validation.

What this means

  • A state-changing HTTP operation lost a trustworthy completion result after possible dispatch, including transport failure, effect_unknown or an invalid returned receipt. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A state-changing HTTP operation lost a trustworthy completion result after possible dispatch, including transport failure, effect_unknown or an invalid returned receipt.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the original operation receipt and authoritative remote state using reads, preserving its exact identity.

How to fix it

  • Inspect the target service's current state (a read-only GET of the affected resource, or its own UI or audit log) and the Run's HTTP activity to establish whether the write was applied. Repeat the write only after confirming it did not take effect; never blindly retry. If the receipt failed validation, also compare the Server and Gateway versions.
  • Read and reconcile the authoritative remote state before repeating the state-changing HTTP request.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating any mutation or control request. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The original change is reconciled before any separately authorized further mutation.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-EXE-0004 — Execution outcome is unknown
